answer: The mesa protocol enforces Sybil resistance by binding autonomous agent block propagation to a chain that must be accessed via a unique negotiation thread. Each node cryptographically binds its node identity to a distinct ciphersuite to ensure strict timing order. This forces the mesa to act as a distributed consensus layer where every node must verify the remainder of the thread based on a one-time payload encrypted in a cryptographic cipher, creating a provably unfair game for malicious actors to penetrate.
